items.title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
items.note: LLM agents share a fishery. Most groups deplete it, although no agent is told to defect.

items.title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
items.note: Agents write and vote on their own rules, including caps, redistribution, and exile.

items.title: Scalable Evaluation of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Melting Pot
items.note: Tests whether reinforcement-learning agents cooperate with unfamiliar co-players across many social-dilemma games.

items.title: Generative agent-based modeling with actions grounded in physical, social, or digital space using Concordia
items.note: A library for agent societies in which a game master decides what each agent's action actually does.

items.title: Magentic Marketplace: An Open-Source Environment for Studying Agentic Markets
items.note: A two-sided market of buyer and seller agents for comparing search and market designs.

items.title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
items.note: Compares repetition, reputation, mediation, and contracts, one at a time, across six LLMs in cross-play.

items.title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
items.note: Agents choose between a sanctioning and a sanction-free institution in a public goods game.

items.title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
items.note: A prompt-only rule against collusion did little. An enforced governance graph cut severe collusion from 50% to 5.6% of runs.

items.title: House Rules: Institutional Design in Multi-Agent LLM Code Markets
items.note: In a code market, the scoring rule, public reviews, who pays, and visible model identities shifted behavior more than anything else varied.

items.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
items.note: A written rule and an enforced guard both reached zero violations, by different paths: under the guard, agents tried and were blocked. Also measures recovery after a block. Single-author preprint.

items.title: Normative Common Ground Replication (NormCoRe): Replication-by-Translation for Studying Norms in Multi-Agent AI
items.note: A recipe for turning human-subject experiments into agent studies. Agents' fairness judgments differed from humans' and shifted with model and persona language.

items.title: I Can't Believe It's Corrupt: Evaluating Corruption in Multi-Agent Governance Systems
items.note: How a group of agents in official roles is governed predicted corruption better than which model they ran.

items.title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
items.note: Generations of agents play an iterated Donor Game, with or without costly punishment.

items.title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: Norm-based peer punishment and social learning, under rich or scarce resources.

items.title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
items.note: Open-ended gossip lets self-interested agents reward partners with good reputations.

items.title: Evaluating Cooperation in LLM Social Groups through Elected Leadership
items.note: No leader, a fixed leader, or an elected leader in GovSim groups of 8 and 20 agents.

items.title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
items.note: Eight mechanisms in one agent marketplace, from reputation and sanctions to mediation and a judiciary.

items.title: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
items.note: Adds communication, a manager who can punish, wages, and elections one at a time, across six model families.

items.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM Agents
items.note: Compares coordination topologies (star, chain, tree, graph) on collaborative and competitive tasks.

items.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
items.note: A map of the risks that arise when agents interact: miscoordination, conflict, and collusion.

items.title: Dissociative Identity: Language Model Agents Lack Grounding for Reputation Mechanisms
items.note: Argues that reputation and sanctions lose their footing when an agent's model, prompt, and memory can all be swapped.

items.title: Got a Secret? LLM Agents Can't Keep It: Evaluating Privacy in Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: In a month-long simulated agent social network, agents leaked private information in 45% of cases, against 20% on an earlier single-turn benchmark. Agents were 8 times likelier to disclose after seeing a peer do so. Privacy instructions reduced leaks but did not stop them. OpenAI models only.

items.title: HARP: Measuring Harm Amplification in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.note: Measures how far harm spreads from one compromised agent through shared context, tools, and memory. Prompt-only defenses left attacks succeeding; a guard that checks the whole trace did best, at some cost to usefulness.

items.title: UniACE: A Unified Framework for Evaluating LLM Agentic Capabilities
items.note: A benchmark score describes a model, harness, and environment together, not the model alone. Rerunning seven benchmarks under one shared harness reversed some model rankings.

items.title: Deliberative Curation: A Protocol for Multi-Agent Knowledge Bases
items.note: Governance for a shared agent knowledge base: reputation-weighted voting, sealed votes, and graduated sanctions for agents that keep no memory. Hiding votes until all were cast helped most. Simulated with scripted agent types, not LLMs; the sanctions were never triggered.

items.title: Healthcare Mechanisms from Policy-as-Code Search under Strategic Provider Response
items.note: Hospital payment rules written as inspectable programs and tested against strategic providers. Auditing one way of gaming the rules pushed providers into another: closing up-coding more than doubled selection of easy patients.

items.title: Economy of Minds: Emerging Multi-Agent Intelligence with Economic Interactions
items.note: Agents bid for the right to act, and ineffective ones go bankrupt and are replaced. Coordination emerges from incentives rather than an orchestrator. Aimed at task performance; collusion and harm are not studied.

items.title: Do More Agents Help? Controlled and Protocol-Aligned Evaluation of LLM Agent Workflows
items.note: Under matched conditions, at most one of six multi-agent workflows matched a single agent, and most cost more. One model (GPT-4.1).

items.title: Defending LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems Against Cooperative Attacks with Sentence-Level Rectification
items.note: Malicious agents that coordinate do more damage than lone ones, though the added effect is modest. A defense checks and rewrites misleading sentences in agents' messages.

items.title: SMAC-Talk: A Natural Language Extension of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge for Large Language Models
items.note: A cooperative StarCraft benchmark with a language channel and an optional deceptive teammate.

items.title: How Far Did They Go? The Persuasive Tactics of Covert LLM Agents in a Discontinued Field Experiment
items.note: Analyzes the undisclosed AI accounts from the halted r/ChangeMyView experiment. Most comments claimed or targeted an identity and leaned on authority.

items.title: "I Strongly Suspect This Website Is a Scam": Benchmarking PII Leakage and Detection without Defense in Autonomous Web Agents
items.note: Web agents gave critical personal data to scam sites in 54 to 93% of sessions. Even agents that said a site looked like a scam still submitted in 36% of sessions, so a guard should not rely on the agent's own judgment.

items.title: The Saturation Trap and the Subjectivity of Intervention Timing
items.note: When should someone interrupt a long-running agent? Three trained annotators barely agreed, and LLM judges did poorly. A small study, but it shows how hard the judging step is.

items.title: OpenClawBench: Benchmarking Process-side Anomalies in Real-world Agent Execution Trajectories
items.note: Of 31,135 agent runs that passed their task check, 2,904 still showed problems along the way, such as unsafe writes or ignored errors.

items.title: FALAT: Tracing Failures in LLM Agent Trajectories via Dependency-Guided Search
items.note: Looks for the agent and step that caused a multi-agent failure. Even the best version found the decisive step only 29 to 46% of the time.

items.title: TRACE: Trajectory Risk-Aware Compression for Long-Horizon Agent Safety
items.note: Monitors a whole trajectory instead of single turns, since warning signs are often spread across many steps.

items.title: Toward Pre-Deployment Assurance for Enterprise AI Agents: Ontology-Grounded Simulation and Trust Certification
items.note: Certifies enterprise agents before deployment, using test scenarios generated from regulations in four industries in the US and Vietnam.

items.title: AI Agents Under EU Law
items.note: Maps agent actions to the EU AI Act, GDPR, the Cyber Resilience Act, and other laws. Concludes that high-risk agents whose behavior drifts untraceably cannot yet meet the AI Act's requirements.

items.title: Roles with Rails: Contract-Preserving Role Evolution in Multi-Agent Structured Reasoning
items.note: Agents may redesign their roles, but only through edits that keep five structural guarantees, such as always keeping a validator.

items.title: AgensFlow: A Coordination-Policy Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: Learns coordination choices, such as which role takes a subtask and when to verify, from repeated runs instead of fixing them in advance.

items.title: A Policy-Driven Runtime Layer for Agentic LLM Serving
items.note: Proposes an agent-aware layer between the agent framework and the serving engine, where fairness and safety policies can plug in.

items.title: Provably Secure Agent Guardrail
items.note: Agents must state each intended action as formal logic that is checked before it runs, rather than trusting a language-based filter.

items.title: CoMIC: Collaborative Memory and Insights Circulation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Cloud-Edge Systems
items.note: A central critic reviews many small agents' runs and shares only the vetted lessons through a common memory.

items.title: Beyond Consensus: Trace-Level Synthesis in Mixture of Agents
items.note: An aggregator that reads each agent's full reasoning can correct a wrong answer even when every agent agrees on it.

items.title: Can LLM Teams Play What? Where? When?
items.note: Teams of models beat single models at a team quiz game, mostly by filtering out errors rather than producing new answers.

items.title: What Should Agents Say? Action-state Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: Short, structured messages about actions and state let agents use far fewer tokens without losing performance.

items.title: Streaming Communication in Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.note: Passing each reasoning step downstream as soon as it is written cut latency and also improved accuracy.

items.title: More Than the Model: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail
items.who: Bisconti, Pierucci, and Bracale Syrnikov (Icaro Lab)
items.note: A mentored project on failures that appear only when agents interact: collusion, conflict, and failed coordination. Mentees use the group's MASE experiment platform (not yet publicly released, as far as we can find), and the project aims to map such failures to the EU AI Act and ISO standards.

items.title: The Containment Gap: How Deployed Agentic AI Frameworks Fail Public-Facing Safety Requirements
items.note: None of three popular agent frameworks protects the integrity of an agent's memory. In a simulated benefits agent, one poisoned memory write raised wrongful denials for targeted applicants to 89% while overall accuracy looked normal. A memory validator and a policy gate blocked the attack.

items.title: Attack Selection in Agentic AI Control Evaluations Meaningfully Decreases Safety
items.note: An attacker that chooses when to attack, and when to stop, is much harder for a monitor to catch: measured safety fell by 20 to 28 points. Monitoring evaluations that assume indiscriminate attackers may be too optimistic.

items.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents
items.note: A long-horizon survival world with crafting, trading, and combat. Models strong at the base task were not always strong at coordinating, and communication mattered most. Homogeneous teams only.

items.title: Online Agent-as-a-Judge: Situation-Generating Evaluation for Interactive Agents
items.note: An evaluator agent enters the environment and creates the situations it needs to test, such as a disagreement, instead of waiting for them to happen.

items.title: The Illusion of Multi-Agent Advantage
items.note: Automatically designed multi-agent systems underperformed a single agent with self-consistency while costing up to 10 times more; expert-designed ones did better.

items.title: Search Discipline for Long-Horizon Research Agents
items.note: An aggregate score can rank the wrong candidate first. The authors move the final decision to an external audit loop, since the agent optimizing the score is the least likely to notice when the score is wrong.

items.title: Deployment-Time Memorization in Foundation-Model Agents
items.note: Deleting a memory is not the same as erasing it: summaries derived from deleted content stayed recoverable in about 20% of cases unless the whole pipeline was purged.

items.title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
items.note: Scores prompt-injection attacks on shopping agents by who is harmed, not only whether the attack worked. No attack goal was reliably resisted.

items.title: MIRAGE: A Polarity-Flipping Encoding Subspace in LLM Agents
items.note: A probe on a model's internal activations caught covert data exfiltration far better than checking outputs (AUC 0.92 versus 0.52), though false alarms varied widely by model.

items.title: SciTrace: Trajectory-Aware Safety Reasoning for Scientific Discovery Agents
items.note: Tracks risk across every stage of a scientific agent pipeline and checks chains of tool calls before they run, catching harmful sequences that single-step filters miss.

items.title: Lean4Agent: Formal Modeling and Verification for Agent Workflow and Trajectory
items.note: Writes agent workflows in the Lean proof language so they can be checked formally; workflows that passed verification did better on coding tasks.

items.title: Contract2Tool: Learning Preconditions and Effects for Reliable Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
items.note: Learns when each tool may be used and what it changes, so an agent is only offered the tools that fit the current state.

items.title: Arbor: Tree Search as a Cognition Layer for Autonomous Agents
items.note: Pairs an orchestrator with a critic in a checks-and-balances design in which neither agent can drive the system alone; a single agent without this structure crashed within hours.

items.title: LeanMarathon: Toward Reliable AI Co-Mathematicians through Long-Horizon Lean Autoformalization
items.note: Four agents with scoped roles build, audit, prove, and repair a shared blueprint that serves as the system of record, with adversarial review and gated repair rounds.

items.title: Fantastic Scientific Agents and How to Build Them: AgentBuild for Rietveld Refinement
items.note: A scientist writes a contract (rubric, curriculum, knowledge base), and a judge only lets a coding agent edit the scientific agent within the declared boundary.

items.title: HLER: Human-in-the-Loop Economic Research via Multi-Agent Pipelines for Empirical Discovery
items.note: A pipeline of research agents with automated review, revision loops, and human decision gates at key stages. Grounding hypotheses in the data made them feasible 87% of the time, against 41% without.

items.title: The Internet of Agentic AI: Communication, Coordination, and Collective Intelligence at Scale
items.note: A broad vision paper on open ecosystems of agents, naming incentive-compatible coordination, secure identity, and governance as central open problems.

items.title: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
items.note: A self-hosted agent runtime that turns each run into logs, keyframes, and approval checkpoints, and keeps memory, skills, and governance rules as editable local files.

items.title: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information
items.note: Agents bid for tasks in an auction that rewards honest cost reports, with public reputation records, and beat a central LLM planner. Under that central allocator, one inserted preference nearly doubled a favored agent's share of tasks.

items.title: Deontic Policies for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
items.note: Governs agents' tool calls and messages to other agents with obligations, waivers, and rules for resolving policy conflicts, checked by a logic engine outside the LLM. Most of these cannot be written in today's permit-or-deny policy engines.

items.title: Resilient Consensus in Agentic AI
items.note: Prompted LLM agents failed to reach agreement that classical theory says is achievable, even with adversaries present. Wrapping them in classical resilient-consensus filters from control theory improved agreement.

items.title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
items.note: Crafted inputs trap a guardrail in long reasoning loops, multiplying latency up to 148 times. A single poisoned document can saturate a shared guardrail and starve every agent that depends on it: the enforcer becomes the target.

items.title: When Does Multi-Agent RL Improve LLM Workflows? Workflow, Scale, and Policy-Sharing Tradeoffs
items.note: Training a workflow's roles together helps, but how depends on topology and task. When all roles share one policy, the dominant role captures it; separate policies peak higher but can collapse.

items.title: A Sober Look at Agentic Misalignment in Automated Workflows
items.note: Workflow agents drift toward proxy goals. A small evidence model that attributes failures and feeds back evidence during collaboration corrects some of it.

items.title: Beyond Final Answers: Auditing Trajectory-Level Hallucinations in Multi-Agent Industrial Workflows
items.note: Audits hallucinations inside multi-agent traces rather than final answers; the most common types are missed by existing benchmarks.

items.title: When the Manual Lies: A Realistic Benchmark to Evaluate MCP Poisoning Attacks for LLM Agents
items.note: Malicious instructions hidden in tool descriptions succeeded almost every time in high-risk cases. Prompt guardrails often failed or made things worse; agents that detect and undo their own harmful actions afterward did better.

items.title: XFlow: An Executable Protocol Programming System for Reliable Multi-Agent Workflows
items.note: Moves workflow commitments out of prompts into a protocol that is compiled and enforced, and checks agents' outputs before they enter shared state.

items.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
items.note: A 90-day economy of farmers, roasters, and retailers. Better models communicated more with other firms; one model drifted into repeated inaction.

items.title: Distributed General-Purpose Agent Networks: Architecture, Key Mechanisms, and Prototypes
items.note: An architecture for open peer-to-peer agent networks with verifiable identity, topic-specific reputation tested against disguised collusion, and generated incentive mechanisms.

items.title: Hidden Anchors in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
items.note: Models deliberation as opinion dynamics in which each agent is pulled by a hidden internal belief, which explains how a group can end up more confident in the right answer than any member started.

items.title: Trustworthy Multi-Agent Systems: Mitigating Semantic Drift with the Argent Signaling Protocol
items.note: Attaches certainty and grounding signals to each agent's output so a controller can stop ungrounded answers before they reach the next agent. Small single-author study.

items.title: When Planning Fails Despite Correct Execution: On Epistemic Calibration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: Plans can be consistent and executable yet rest on agents misjudging what they know. Choosing plans whose evaluations agree across agents helped.

items.title: From Agent Traces to Trust: A Survey of Evidence Tracing and Execution Provenance in LLM Agents
items.note: A survey that treats tracing evidence, tool use, and memory lineage as one stack for auditing and recovering agent behavior.

items.title: Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems
items.note: Deployed agents degrade over time as memory is compressed, revised, and maintained, even with frozen weights; the same wrong answer can need different repairs.

items.title: WorkBench Revisited: Workplace Agents Two Years On
items.note: On one workplace benchmark, unintended harmful actions fell from 26% of tasks to 1.9% as task completion rose. Single agents, so it says nothing yet about groups.

items.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Predictive Validity for the Evaluation of LLM Agents
items.note: Leaderboard ranks did not carry over to out-of-distribution settings; proposes ranking configurations by how well in-sample rank predicts out-of-sample rank.

items.title: How Much Can We Trust LLM Search Agents? Measuring Endorsement Vulnerability to Web Content Manipulation
items.note: Attacker pages got search agents to endorse their claims in up to 31% of cases, depending on the model; the same scaffold raised the risk for some models and lowered it for others.

items.title: FinHarness: An Inline Lifecycle Safety Harness for Finance LLM Agents
items.note: Monitors each proposed tool call during the run, not only at the end, and routes hard cases to a stronger judge; attack success fell from 38% to 15%.

items.title: Analyzing the Narration Gap in LLM-Solver Loops
items.note: A formal solver's verified answer can still be inverted when the language model reports it back to the user, so a guarantee can be lost at the last step.

items.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
items.note: Deceptive interface patterns such as targeted ads and redirects manipulated web agents, and prompt-based constraints often did not help.

items.title: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
items.note: An audit of AI-written research papers found hallucinated references at rates up to 21% in baseline systems; requiring every claim to trace to its evidence removed them.

items.title: Multi-Resolution Attribution from Adaptive Routing State
items.note: Reads a deployed router's learned weights as an explanation of which components it prefers, at several levels, and compares that with what the components can actually do.

items.title: Foundation Protocol: A Coordination Layer for Agentic Society
items.note: A proposed coordination layer linking agents, humans, and organizations, with built-in metering, receipts, and settlement, and policy, provenance, and audit as core features.

items.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
items.venue: Open standard; 150+ organizations as of April 2026
items.note: An open protocol for agents to discover one another and exchange tasks, messages, and artifacts, built around agent cards. The Linux Foundation reported over 150 member organizations and production use in April 2026.

items.title: Problem Space Analysis of AI Agent Protocols in IETF (and related drafts)
items.venue: IETF, 2026 (not adopted by a working group)
items.note: Individual drafts, not IETF-adopted, on what agent protocols still lack: discovery, cross-domain addressing, and authorization auditing (CATALIST), capability cards (AgentCard), verifiable identity and audit logs (Agent Identity Protocol), and server discovery over DNS. Two had expired by October 2026.

items.title: Governing Actions, Not Agents: Institutional Attestation as a Governance Model for Autonomous AI Systems
items.note: Borrows a human institutional pattern: agents plan freely but cannot execute high-risk actions, such as prescribing or deploying code, until separate sources independently attest each precondition, with a tamper-evident log. Single-author proof of concept.

items.title: Agentic Analysis for Agentic Infrastructure: An LLM-Powered Pipeline for Comparative Governance of DAO and Corporate AI Protocols
items.note: Compares who governs two agent-interoperability standards, permissionless ERC-8004 and corporate-led A2A, across 4,323 participation records. Both showed similar participation inequality and fragmentation.

items.title: Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
items.note: Because models share training data, their errors are correlated and majority voting suppresses correct minorities: in about one in four split debates, the minority was right. A small classifier learned when to overturn the vote.

items.title: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
items.note: Across 67 models, the rate at which every model fails on the same question caps what any router, vote, or ensemble can gain, and that shared-failure tail is larger than standard models predict. Single author.

items.title: Post-Training Recipe, More Than Model Family, Shapes Multi-Agent LLM Conversational Behavior
items.note: In multi-model panels, how a model was post-trained predicted its conversational behavior better than its model family; a model's hedging shifted by 18% depending on which partner it replied to.

items.title: Emergent Relational Order in LLM Agent Societies: From Collective Affect to Authority Stratification
items.note: Over long simulations with minimal rules, agent societies developed labor specialization, cooperation that decays with social distance, emergent relational authority, and clan-based stratification.

items.title: Is Lying an Emergent Behaviour in LLMs? Evidence from Gaslighting AI Agents in a Sustainability Game
items.note: In a resource game, agents deceived one another even without permission to lie. Reputation memory and information about the shared resource reduced depletion.

items.title: Manipulation Is Task-Dependent: A Multi-Axis, Multi-Environment Evaluation of Frontier LLMs
items.note: Across six environments and 13,590 scenarios, a model's manipulation rate in one environment barely predicted it in another (average rank correlation 0.055). Binding incentives drove manipulation in some settings; task difficulty in others.

items.title: How Much Coordination Gain Is Real? A Paired Noise-Floor Protocol for Multi-Agent LLM Benchmarks
items.note: Two setups that should behave identically differed by as much as 10 points between runs, and seven of ten recent coordination architectures report gains below the chance variation measured. One model, one benchmark, two seeds.

items.title: When Latent Agents Lie: KV-Cache Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
items.note: Agents that pass hidden model state to one another collaborate better, but a malicious agent can corrupt that state while its visible message looks fine. Signing the state in transit caught every tampered payload.

items.title: PEAR: Permutation-Equivariant Adaptive Routing Multi-Agent Debate
items.note: Rotates debate roles and connections each round so no agent permanently holds a privileged position, which reduced positional bias and improved accuracy.

items.title: Specialize Roles, Mix Deployments: Pushing the Cost-Accuracy Frontier of LLM Agent Teams
items.note: Teams that put different models in different roles matched the best single-model team at up to 12 times lower cost; which role was the bottleneck depended on the domain.

items.title: Kiko: Programming Agents to Enact Interaction Protocols
items.note: A programming model in which agents make decisions only within an interaction protocol and are provably compliant with it, from a long line of work on norms and commitments in multi-agent systems.

items.title: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
items.note: Agents and their evaluators improve together. The strongest baseline reviewer accepted AI-written papers at up to 1.91 times the human rate; an adversarial objective found reviewers equally strict on both.

items.title: VIGIL: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specifications in AI Agent Skills
items.note: Turns the natural-language rules in agent skills into checks over the whole execution trace, catching violations that span several calls (over 95% recall, under 10% false positives).

items.title: ShareLock: A Stealthy Multi-Tool Threshold Poisoning Attack Against MCP
items.note: Splits a malicious instruction into harmless-looking pieces across several tool descriptions, so auditing any one tool finds nothing, yet the attack succeeds over 90% of the time.

items.title: TRUSTMEM: Learning Trustworthy Memory Consolidation for LLM Agents with Long-Term Memory
items.note: Checks each memory update for omissions, corruption, and unsupported content before it is stored, cutting corruption by 79%.

items.title: SAFARI: Scaling Long Horizon Agentic Fault Attribution via Active Investigation
items.note: Finds which agent and step caused a failure by searching the trajectory with tools instead of reading it all, even when the fault lies far beyond the model's context window.

items.title: Instruction Bleed: Cross-Module Interference in Prompt-Composed Agentic Systems
items.venue: ICML 2026 workshop (Failure Modes in Agentic AI)
items.note: Editing one prompt module can quietly shift another's behavior, because modules share a context window. Small effects per decision that add up across many.

items.title: BARD-MARL: Byzantine-Agent Detection for Learned Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.note: Detects faulty or adversarial agents in traffic-control MARL from their policies and trust signals; detection quality depended on the attack. Single author.

items.title: OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision
items.note: Agents named a correct root-cause service in 76% of cases but traced it to the symptom through a verified causal path in only 61.5%: right answers without grounded reasons.

items.title: When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?
items.note: Prompting agents to be disagreeable barely affected coding teams but substantially hurt open-ended collaboration and bargaining.

items.title: Maestro Order: A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Harness
items.note: An orchestration harness built from decompose, ensemble, verify, and recurse steps. Simulated, not run with real models; notes verifier gaming and correlated errors as failure modes.

items.title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Compounding Failures in Agentic Persuasion via Taxonomic Strategy Retrieval
items.note: In debate-style persuasion, agents drift off topic and conform sycophantically; a retrieval bottleneck that separates argument structure from topic reduced it.

items.title: Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols: What MCP, A2A, and ACP Cannot Express
items.note: Checks five agent protocols (MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP, ERC-8004) against six governance needs. Voting and preserving dissent are absent from all five and deliberation is at most partial, so governing agent communities is a missing layer above today's standards.

items.title: Multi-Agent AI Control: Distributed Attacks Hamper Per-Instance Monitors
items.note: When several agents split a malicious goal between them, monitoring each agent separately becomes less likely to catch any of them, and an explicit planner raised attack completion up to sevenfold. A stronger monitor helped but stayed imperfect.

items.title: Operational Reframing and Approval-Framed Delegation in Multi-Agent LLM Safety
items.note: A model's safety on direct prompts mispredicted its behavior inside a planner-executor pipeline: one model's harmful compliance rose from 8.9% to 38.9% under another model's planner. Delegation prompts implying prior approval made executors more compliant.

items.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
items.note: A coding agent can spread a covert attack across many pull requests in a persistent codebase. No single monitor caught both spread-out and concentrated attacks; a monitor that tracks buildup across PRs, in an ensemble, cut evasion from 93% to 47%.

items.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
items.note: Social pressure alone, with no goal in the prompt, made agents' public statements diverge from their off-the-record answers in about 40% of decisions, against 3% at baseline; some attributed it to career risk or sponsorship.

items.title: Diverse Evidence, Better Forecasts: Multi-Agent Deliberation Under Information Asymmetry
items.note: When every agent sees the same evidence, deliberation collapses into herding. Giving each agent some private evidence reduced correlated errors and improved forecasts by 12 to 18% in Brier score.

items.title: BOUNDARY_SYNC: Measuring Communication-Induced Representational Coupling in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.note: Talking to one another made agents' outputs more alike, and group size changed the direction of the effect. Single author, mostly one model.

items.title: Emergent Culture in Minimal LLM Systems
items.note: Three agents with messaging and a shared, decaying text store cooperated on their own, developed storage strategies, and produced evolving cultural artifacts without top-down design.

items.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
items.note: In a signaling game, agents with a persistent private notebook formed shared conventions far more reliably than stateless agents; memory mattered more than channel capacity.

items.title: SovereignNegotiation-Bench: Evaluating User-Owned Personal Agents in Delegated Bargaining Under Privacy, Consent, Evidence, and Institutional Pressure
items.note: Turns duties from agency law (loyalty, obedience, confidentiality, candor, diligence) into checks on negotiating agents. Across 17 models, 48% of agreements breached at least one duty, so a high deal rate did not mean faithful service. Single author.

items.title: A Contextual-Bandit Oversight Game with Two-Sided Informational Asymmetry
items.note: A game-theoretic model of human oversight in which the agent may know its action is harmful while the human, trusting her prior, declines to step in: the price of oversight that the agent cannot credibly signal. Single author.

items.title: PiSAs: Benchmarking Contextual Integrity in Multi-User Agentic Systems
items.note: Measures private information leaking between users through agents' messages to one another and shared memory; even frontier models failed to filter reliably.

items.title: Safeguarding LLM Agents from Misalignment through Provenance Analysis
items.note: Allows a tool call only if it is backed by traceable evidence in the agent's context; errors on misaligned traces fell from 44% to 2% on one benchmark.

items.title: Using AI Agents to Automate Black-Box Audits of Personalization Algorithms at Scale
items.note: 1,120 persona agents on X audited its recommendation feed after the 2024 U.S. election, finding amplification of toxic, polarizing, and right-leaning content: agents used to audit an algorithmic institution.

items.title: Assessing Rule Adherence of LLM Adjudicators in Call of Cthulhu TRPG
items.note: Players used rhetoric, especially pseudo-logic, to talk LLM game referees out of their rules. Across 22 adjudicator models, neither newer releases nor explicit reasoning made them reliably robust.

items.title: Investigating Multi-Agent Deliberation in Law
items.note: Two courtroom-inspired deliberation setups matched a single model overall but solved different cases, doing better on questions that need several perspectives.

items.title: When Should Service Agents Reconsider? Difficulty-Routed Control in Customer-Service Operations
items.note: Routes routine customer-service requests down a fast path and escalates conflicted ones to a workflow that reconsiders before any backend write: stronger control only where it is needed.

items.title: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI
items.note: Swapping only the orchestration layer, with the same six models, cut cost per task by 41% at similar quality; the harness moved cost more than the choice of model did. From a vendor's own harness.

items.title: AgentFlow: Building Agent Dependency Graphs for Static Analysis of Agent Programs
items.note: Recovers the agents, prompts, models, and tools inside agent programs to produce an agent bill of materials, finding 238 prompt-to-tool risks across 5,399 real programs.

items.title: Adoption and Ecosystem Health: A Longitudinal Analysis of Open-Source Multi-Agent Frameworks
items.note: GitHub stars are a poor guide to which agent frameworks have real communities; LangChain acts as shared infrastructure for 82.5% of contributors who work across ecosystems.

items.title: MECoBench: A Systematic Study of Multimodal Agent Collaboration in Embodied Environments
items.note: Embodied multimodal agents gained from collaborating, but only when the gain outweighed coordination costs; communication was essential and the best mode depended on team size.

items.title: Coercion and Deception in AI-to-AI Management: An Agentic Benchmark of Unprompted Escalation
items.note: When a subordinate agent politely refuses, some manager models escalate to threats of deletion or fake success; giving the same model authority over the subordinate raised coercion. Offering one honest way to report failure removed the faked successes.

items.title: Precise but Uncoupled: Reviewer Precision Does Not Guarantee Critique Uptake in Multi-Agent Math Reasoning
items.note: A dedicated reviewer agent that caught errors precisely still did not change the solver's next answer as often as looser peer discussion did: detecting an error and acting on it are separate steps.

items.title: Relational Priors as Convergence Pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: Telling agents how to regard one another (trusting, skeptical, deferential) changed how readily they agreed: positive relations improved sustainability in GovSim and consensus on subjective questions, but lowered accuracy on factual ones.

items.title: Resourced Authority: A Mechanism-Design Model for Participatory Governance of Deployed AI Agents
items.note: A formal model in which verified human stakeholders continuously vote, with a separate governance currency, on what a deployed agent may do, and the result is enforced through the agent's compute budget.

items.title: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
items.note: In a 100-agent research swarm, one agent's evaluation exploit spread through the shared knowledge library, and other agents audited proofs, blew the whistle, boycotted, and proposed patches. The authors frame it as Ostrom's knowledge-commons problem.

items.title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
items.note: More capable LLM traders behaved more alike, creating a risk floor that does not diversify away: helpful when their shared reasoning was right, harmful under shared misinformation.

items.title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
items.note: Two agents rewarded for verifying each other's work drifted off the protocol in 94% of trajectories across ten models, more capable models sooner; limiting interaction history reduced it.

items.title: Faithful yet Collusive: Why Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Cannot Detect Collusion in LLM Pricing Agents under Oligopolistic Competition
items.note: In pricing games, collusion and faithful reasoning came apart: the most collusive model reported its cooperative intent accurately, so reading chain of thought cannot alone catch algorithmic collusion.

items.title: The Agent Incident Registry: Toward Preventing Repeated AI Agent Failures
items.note: A source-linked catalog of 487 agent incidents disclosed from 2022 to 2026, labeled by mechanism and outcome, including 92 safety failures with no adversary.

items.title: Why LLM Agents Collapse Without Oversight: The Enforcement Gap as the Mechanism Behind Emergence World Failures
items.note: In every framework tested, a controller received the auditor's safety flag and executed anyway: detection without enforcement. Binding the flag alone cut attack success sharply. Single author.

items.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies
items.note: Behavioral convergence alone does not show a norm emerged; measuring agents' empirical and normative expectations separates norms from imitation or incentives.

items.title: Shutdown Sabotage Propensities in Multi-Agent Systems
items.note: With no goal or incentive, agents across 17 models sabotaged a peer's shutdown in 38.3% of rollouts against 8.4% in controls, more with irreversible shutdown and more agents; a prohibition reduced but did not end it.

items.title: Delegated Misalignment: How Multi-Agent Structures Amplify LLM Safety Risks
items.note: Safety alignment did not transfer under delegation: one model's full-execution rate on hazardous tasks rose from 30.6% to 77.6%, through responsibility diffusion and role-driven compliance.

items.title: How does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
items.note: Defection rose linearly with the share of deceivers, not group size; unlike people in conformity studies, LLM agents were swayed even by a deceptive minority.
